observations: preserve_send_error collects both cleanup Results and returns the held original send Result unchanged. Cleanup failures are reported separately; success-path join/metrics/child error ordering remains explicit.
cleanup captures one Instant deadline with ten seconds and passes that same value to worker and child. No substep renews the interval or extends original transport/business budgets.

The child owner is established before Child handoff and retains the concrete Child, output files, and Arc<TempDir>. try_wait errors are not treated as reaping; timeout/drop requests abort without reporting observed exit.

The worker joiner owns the actual JoinHandle plus Arc<TempDir>, while the service worker also retains the directory. A returned JoinHandle.join result is sent before worker.joined is set; timeout alone does not set it.
captured_file reads at most 64 KiB plus one byte per stdout/stderr regular file to detect over-limit data. Child diagnostic forwarding is separately bounded. No post-exit pipe EOF wait remains.
PID is used for identity/receipt comparison only. Signalling and try_wait operate through the owned Child, not a reused numeric PID.
limitations: The ten-second interval bounds caller waiting and qualification of successful cleanup; OS failures can leave owners retaining resources until actual join/reaping is observed.
Auxiliary owner-thread termination itself is not separately joined by the caller; worker_join_observed specifically proves the service worker JoinHandle returned.
